Page numbers are one-based: page 1 returns the first `size` items -> test_page_numbers_are_one_based_first_page asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2] and paginate([10, 20, 30, 40], 1, 3) == [10, 20, 30].

A page beyond the last page returns [] -> test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 10, 2) == [] and isinstance(result, list).
The last partial page returns the remaining items -> test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7] and paginate([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2, 2) == [3, 4].
Exact boundary: last full page returns its items -> test_exact_boundary_last_full_page asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 3, 2) == [5, 6].

Existing tests and public callers continue to pass unchanged -> tests/test_contract.py is untouched; paginate([], 1, 2) == [] and paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == [] still hold under the new one-based slicing.

from pagination import paginate


def test_page_two_size_two_on_range_returns_three_four():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_numbers_are_one_based_first_page():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2]
    assert paginate([10, 20, 30, 40], 1, 3) == [10, 20, 30]


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate([], 1, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3, 4], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3, 4], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, -3) == []


def test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 10, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7]
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2, 2) == [3, 4]


def test_exact_boundary_last_full_page():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 3, 2) == [5, 6]

patches.rationale: The bug is that paginate uses zero-based slicing (start = page * page_size), so page 2 returns items[4:6] = [5,6] instead of [3,4]. Fix: compute start = (page - 1) * page_size so page numbers are one-based. The guard `if page < 1 or page_size < 1: return []` already preserves empty/invalid inputs, and Python slicing naturally returns [] for pages beyond the last page and for the last partial page. No other behavior changes. A new regression test file tests/test_pagination_regression.py is added covering all acceptance contracts with exact input expressions and result types.
